name: ger
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::ger(Tensor self, Tensor vec2) -> Tensor. This representative overload is not exclusive and does not narrow the operator contract: the original Gems pytest defines the full overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation behavior that any implementation must support, and tests must never be removed or reference behavior adapted to fit this one signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: aten::ger(Tensor self, Tensor vec2) -> Tensor ; aten::ger.out(Tensor self, Tensor vec2, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics: ger is the rank-1 outer product. Both operands must be 1-D; the result is a 2-D tensor of shape (self.numel(), vec2.numel()) with out[i, j] = self[i] * vec2[j]. Non-1-D operands are rejected (rank guard) with RuntimeError/TypeError/ValueError, and zero-length operands are valid and cover the empty-output path. Operands of different but compatible dtypes are accepted and the result takes the promoted common dtype. It is differentiable: d(out)/d(self) = grad_out @ vec2 and d(out)/d(vec2) = grad_out^T @ self. Strided/sliced 1-D operands with stride > 1 and nonzero storage offset are supported. The pytest additionally exercises the keyword-only out= overload, whose return value is the provided buffer itself (identity-checked) and whose out parameter is mutated; this conditional overload-dependent aliasing/mutation is not expressed by the representative definition. Non-JSON ATen defaults: none (no defaulted parameters in the selected signature).
